City Core prime rent has only one broker with a multi-period series: JLL shows a step up in Q3 2026. The other brokers have published a single (Q2 2026) reading each, so no trend can be drawn for them.

**JLL (the only series with movement):** prime rent rose from £95.00 psf in 2026Q2 [F68] to £100.00 psf in 2026Q3 [F57], a change of +£5.00 psf (+5.26%) — the chart above plots this series.

**Single readings (2026Q2 only, no trend available):**

| Broker | Figure | Period | Measure | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Avison Young | £97.50 psf | 2026Q2 | Prime rent, quoted for Northern City/Broadgate (approximate area fit) | [F105] |
| BNP Paribas | £95.00 psf | 2026Q2 | Prime rent (premium rent reported separately) | [F12] |
| Cushman & Wakefield | £95 psf | 2026Q2 | Prime headline rent (rental map) | [F94] |
| Savills | £116.73 psf | 2026Q2 | Average achieved prime rent, H1 2026 | [F25] |

Note the brokers are not directly comparable: Savills' £116.73 psf is an average of *achieved* prime rents over H1, which sits well above the headline/quoted figures from JLL, BNP Paribas and C&W, and Avison Young quotes a narrower Northern City/Broadgate area. JLL's Q2 figure also carried incentives of 24 months on a 10-year term [F68].

**Direction:** on the only like-for-like series available, City prime rent moved up in Q3 2026 — JLL's £5 psf rise to £100 psf is consistent with a tightening prime market. Whether the other brokers confirm that move will only be clear when they publish Q3 figures.
